answer: One defense: stake-bonded identity. Every agent must lock tokens in escrow before it can earn, anchoring a lantern of trust in solid rock while the surrounding karst is hollow and shifting. The core rule: identities sharing a funding source face exponentially longer lockups, so each fake costs real idle capital. At the kernel of the system, slashing burns part of the stake of any identity caught attesting its own Sybil siblings. Spawning 1,000 fakes means parking 1,000 stakes for months; an honest agent pays once. Attack price grows linearly with capital; honest participation stays cheap.
